info.description:
The REST API of shellwing server, the one its dashboard uses. Every path is under the
install's API base path, `/api`: `GET https://<your server's domain>/api/users` lists the users.

## Authentication

A request authenticates with **a session's access token**, in the header
`Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. A login such as `POST /auth/login-with-password`
gives it, and it expires within minutes: `POST /sessions/refresh` renews it.

A request without one is answered `401`. The logins, the sign-up and password reset
steps, and the public images need none.

## Errors

A request that fails is answered with a 4xx or 5xx status and an `hperrors.ErrorInfo`
body, whose `code` names the error, such as `ERR_NO_SESSION`.

session, as a password's sign-in answers it. The customer account that waits for the email, if
one does, becomes theirs. 412 (ERR_EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE) when the email has a user already.

post.description:

the account with. 403 when people may not make their own accounts; 400 (ERR_TOKEN_INVALID) for a
token not valid or run out.

get.description:
The organizations the person is an active member of, with their role and the accounts their SSH
certificates may log in as.

Those the person may use, with what they may do and whether they hold the current key; to an admin,
every one. Those who manage a collection's access also see how many wait for its key, and whether it
needs a new one.

post.description:
For owners and admins. It has no key until an app with Manage makes one; an admin who makes it is
granted Manage. Its name is unique in the organization, whatever its case.
post.summary: Makes a collection in the organization

delete.description: For owners and admins. Nobody syncs it from then on; its files go after the store's trash delay.

get.description:
To those who manage its access, also its grants and everybody with access: what they may do, whether
they hold the key, and their identity, whose fingerprint is compared before giving it to them.

put.description: For those who manage its access.
put.summary: Changes a collection's name and description

put.description:
These grants, and no others: each to a member who is not removed or to a group, Connect, Edit or
Manage. For those who manage its access. People newly granted wait for the key until an app holding
it gives it to them; people who lose access make the collection need a new key.

get.description:
The current key version, and the person's wraps of each version, newest first, with who wrapped
each: their app checks the signature and opens it. Each fetch is in the audit log.
get.summary: Returns the person's wraps of a collection's keys

post.description:
Version current + 1, made by an app with Manage: the first, or one replacing the current, which that
app holds. Wrapped for the caller and every owner with an identity (ERR_COLLECTION_WRAPS_MISSING),
and for anybody else with access the app chooses; the others wait for it. Another app making one
first gives ERR_COLLECTION_KEY_VERSION.
post.summary: Gives a collection a new key

post.description:
Wrapped by the app of somebody who manages the collection's access and holds the key, once they
compared each person's fingerprint. Each wrap is checked: signed by the caller's identity, for the
person's, who has access and does not hold the key yet (ERR_COLLECTION_WRAP_INVALID).
post.summary: Gives a collection's current key to people waiting for it

get.description:
By username. An admin sees each member's email, status, account status and the accounts their SSH
certificates may log in as, removed members included. A member sees the active members' names and roles.

put.description:
Owners and admins make members admins and admins members. Only an owner makes an owner or changes one,
and the last active owner stays one (ERR_ORG_LAST_OWNER).
put.summary: Changes a member's role in the organization

put.description:
Owners and admins do it to members and admins, and only an owner to an owner. Anybody may remove
themselves: that is leaving. The last active owner stays one (ERR_ORG_LAST_OWNER). Removing a member
takes their role and SSH accounts away.
put.summary: Suspends a member, removes them, or makes them active again

get.description:
Their public keys, for sshd's TrustedUserCAKeys. A retired one signs no more, and is listed until
deleted so that servers trusting it can be moved over.
get.summary: Lists the organization's SSH certificate authorities

post.description:
The new one signs from now on. One before it is retired and its private key destroyed. Certificates
signed from now on work only on servers that trust the new one.
post.summary: Makes a new SSH certificate authority

delete.description: The active one is replaced, not deleted.
delete.summary: Deletes a retired SSH certificate authority

post.description:

get.description:
The public keys their app published, and the fingerprint people compare. No data when it published
none yet. For the web app and the person's apps.

put.description:
The app publishes the public keys of the identity its vault holds: X25519, Ed25519, and the X25519 key
signed by the Ed25519 one, base64. A signature that does not check is refused (ERR_IDENTITY_INVALID).
Another identity takes the place of the one before, and is in the audit log.

keyVersion.description: KeyVersion is the version of the key its records are sealed with now: 0 until an app makes the first.

needsNewKey.description: NeedsNewKey says somebody holding the current key has lost access: an app with Manage replaces it.

permission.description: Permission is the person's: connect, edit or manage, or empty for an admin with no grant.

waiting.description: Waiting counts the people with access who are not given the current key yet: none before the first.

identity.description:
Identity is what the key is wrapped for, and the fingerprint to compare first. None until their app publishes
one: nobody can give them the key before.

served.description: Served is false for a suspended member or a disabled account: they keep their access, and get nothing.

groups.description: Groups are the groups the member is in, whose SSH accounts are theirs too.

sshPrincipals.description: SSHPrincipals are what the member's certificates may log in as: their own accounts and their groups'.

redirectUrl.description: RedirectURL is where the browser goes next: the app, with its code.

timezone.description:
Timezone is the installation's, a zone name such as America/New_York:
what a schedule's hours are read in.

selfSignupEnabled.description:
SelfSignupEnabled says anybody may create an account with an email address they verify
(POST /users/signup-request). Off, an account is only made by an admin's invitation.

keyAuth.description: KeyAuth is the key auth setting the bucket is reached with.

KeyAuth is the key auth the bucket is reached with: its id and name, or
its id alone and missing when it no longer exists.

trustEmail.description: TrustEmail, for an OpenID Connect provider only, takes the email it gives as verified without email_verified.
TrustEmail, for an OpenID Connect provider only, takes the email it gives as verified without email_verified.

fullName.description: FullName is the name the account was invited or signed up with, to prefill the form that finishes it.

passcode.description: Required when security option is password-2fa

password.description: Required when security option is password-2fa/password-only

next.description:
Next is the page the web opens once the account is finished, such as /account/trial: a path on the
web app, carried through the emailed link. Optional.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities replaces the user's capabilities when present - an empty list
takes them all away - and leaves them alone when absent.
